summary: Range lights of 1898 guiding vessels into the Annandale river; the 1901 rear tower, PEI's tallest range light, was moved inland in 2020.

evidence.quote: Its unusually tall height and slender profile make it the tallest range light on Prince Edward Island.
Annandale Rear Range Lighthouse is a 19.8 metre (65 feet) tapered, wooden tower
guides vessels into the Boughton River from the Northumberland Strait
At the turn of the 20th century, the Island lacked a land transport route, with goods such as potatoes being exported by water.
Its height, distinctive proportions, and red and white colours make it visible from all vantage points in the village of Annandale.
the Annandale Range Lights were established on land purchased from Alfred Robertson, and George and Edwin McFarlane at a cost of $80

All this work was done under the supervision of Milton Walsh, foreman of works and general repairs for the Department of Marine and Fisheries on Prince Edward Island, at a cost of $2,705.55.

In 1905, Milton Walsh returned to the station an enclosed the rear range light tower, giving it its present appearance. The front range light was relocated to a new site in 1917 by J. M. Morrow under a contract for $70.
At some point, the original front range tower was replaced by the present square, pyramidal tower
The range lights were electrified in June 1960, and Chester Banks was appointed as a caretaker at an annual salary of $100
In 1988, the Annandale Back Range Light was sheathed and reshingled. The rear range lighthouse was discontinued in 2015, and the front light was made a sector light
In February 2020, the government moved the rear range tower roughly 30 metres inland to protect the lighthouse from an eroding bank.

notes_for_editor: Thin-to-moderate evidence. Keeper roster after 1912 rests on LighthouseFriends and the PEI Lighthouse Society (secondary); Andrew Banks 1936-64 and Robertson's 1922-36 return are LighthouseFriends only. J. Norton and his 12 July 1912 date were matched by column position in OCR of the 1913-14 table (Alberton, Annandale range ... columns); quotes there are the unmatched name block. Source 3 is cited by volume (Sessional Papers 1901) because the report's fiscal-year label is unclear given an October 1900 event. Sources differ on whether the rear light is still lit (LF: discontinued 2015; PEI society: active, older). LF says first lit 26 Aug 1898; the 1902-03 table appeared to list an appointment of 5 Oct 1898 but columns were not verified, so omitted. Parks Canada page itself fetched empty; statement of significance read via HistoricPlaces.ca copy. Ownership of the rear tower today (Annandale Lighthouse Inc. vs Crown) not established. Uncited line: front-light height/sector details omitted. Checker: J. Norton, July 12 1912 confirmed on the page image (1914 table, scan 75). The two Alfred Robertson stints are not shown to be one person.
